messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: P1 - inference GPU pool exhausted (us-east-1-b). Autoscaling not responding; worker queue growing rapidly (>1200). Runbook link: /runbooks/gpu_autoscale_failure. Paging oncall. :rotating_light:

oncall-ml: Acked. Jumping in, running quick checks.

sre-ana: On it. First pass: `kubectl get hpa -n inference inference-gpu -o yaml` and `kubectl get pods -n monitoring prometheus-adapter-*`.

eng-ml-raj: Noticed recent prometheus-adapter config change from earlier today (deploy 1796000000) that added a scrape relabel_rules change. Adapter pods show CrashLoopBackOff. Logs: `Error: failed to init client: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` then `panic: runtime error: invalid memory address` in some versions.

oncall-ml: HPA output: currentReplicas=8 desiredReplicas=8 maxReplicas=50, but customMetric "inference_gpu_queue_length" missing -> HPA falls back to cpu metric? It did not scale for the last spike. `kubectl describe hpa inference-gpu` shows: "no metrics available" entries.

sre-ana: Checking cluster-autoscaler logs: scale-up requests sent but cloud API returning `QuotaExceeded: GPU_FAMILY_A quota reached for project`. Also a few nodes failed to provision due to an instance template mismatch (taints in new nodepool prevented scheduling).

infra-ops-sam: Confirming cloud console: GPU quota at 100/100. We have a request for quota increase open but not approved yet. There are also two recently created node pools with `NoSchedule` taints from a bot that was testing node isolation earlier today. I'm removing those taints and calling cloud support for emergency bump.

eng-ml-raj: Workaround: we can patch the prometheus-adapter deployment to previous working image and restart to restore custom metrics. Patch command I'm going to run: ```
kubectl -n monitoring set image deployment/prometheus-adapter prometheus-adapter=redwood/p-adapter:stable-1.9.2
kubectl -n monitoring rollout restart deployment/prometheus-adapter
```

obs-bot: Dashboards: https://dash.re.redwood/inference/queues - GPU queue_length peak 1,420 at 15:12 UTC, 99th latency jumped to 62s, error rate (5xx) 9% over 10m. Alert fired: GPU-pool-utilization-high and GPU-queue-length > 500.

oncall-ml: Applying image revert now.

eng-ml-raj: Revert applied; adapter pods coming up. Logs now show successful metrics POST to HPA endpoint. But note: adapter scrape lag ~9m while backfill runs.

sre-ana: Even with adapter back, cluster-autoscaler requests still failing because of quota. Manual scale attempts to create GPU nodes result in cloud error: `QuotaExceeded`.

infra-ops-sam: Support confirmed emergency quota bump is possible; I've requested a +30 GPUs temporary burst and asked for manual node creation to unblock scheduling. Ticket INFRA-789 opened and priority escalated. ETA unknown but support gave initial ack.

product-ops-claire: Customer impact? Which customers and SLAs?

customer-success-lina: Two enterprise customers reported job failures and timeouts (tickets #CT-3601, #CT-3604). One customer runs latency-critical routing and saw increased tail latency; engineering liaison notified. We're triaging and offering failover suggestions.

oncall-ml: Applying routing mitigation: move low-priority batch to cpu-fallback queue and reduce concurrency for heavy routes to preserve capacity for critical requests. Command (gateway patch): ```
curl -s -X PATCH "https://internal-api/re-routing" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"route":"/v1/infer","low_priority":"cpu-fallback","max_concurrency":2}'
```

obs-bot: After routing change: queue_length down to 420 in 8m. Latency p95 reduced to 18s. Error rate down to 2.6%.

sre-ana: Temporary HPA change proposed: add a secondary metric based on node GPU allocatable instead of only custom metric so we don't fully depend on adapter. Patch preview: ```
kubectl patch hpa inference-gpu -n inference --type='json' -p='[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/metrics/-","value":{"type":"Resource","resource":{"name":"cpu","target":{"type":"Utilization","averageUtilization":70}}}}]'
``` Doing this to nudge scaling while quota resolves.

oncall-ml: Applied. HPA shows desiredReplicas=12 now. Some pods schedule onto existing GPU nodes but many still Pending.

infra-ops-sam: Cloud support provisioned 20 temporary GPUs; creating nodes now. Also removed `NoSchedule` taints from test nodepools. Should begin to see Pending pods schedule within next 6-8 minutes.

obs-bot: Metrics: Pending pods reduced from 9 -> 2 in 10m. GPU queue_length trending to 120. Good recovery path.

customer-success-lina: Customers confirm reduced failures; one still seeing timeouts on older batch jobs queued before mitigation. We're communicating ETA for full catch-up.

product-ops-claire: Adding this to postmortem: runbook lacked immediate step to fallback to CPU and HPA lacked secondary metrics. Also need runbook step for contacting cloud quota team.

sre-ana: Follow-ups: 1) Roll back prometheus-adapter config change and add integration test for TLS cert rotations. 2) Add alert: prometheus-adapter restarts > 3 in 5m. 3) Add quota buffer: reserve 20% capacity or pre-provision burst pool. 4) Add runbook step to consider HPA resource fallback sooner.

eng-ml-raj: I'll produce a hotfix PR for the adapter config and add a canary pipeline. Also will add backfill job to push recent metrics to adapter so HPA has fresher data sooner after restarts.

infra-ops-sam: I'll pursue permanent quota increase and create a reserved burst nodepool for emergencies. Also cleaning up node templates to avoid accidental taints.

incident-bot: Incident created P1-1796024680. Postmortem meeting scheduled: https://wiki.redwood/incidents/P1-1796024680. Owners assigned: SRE (ana) for autoscaler/runbook, ENG-ML (raj) for adapter fix, Infra (sam) for quota/reservation.

oncall-ml: Handoff: I'm leaving channel, handing off to @sre-ana at 16:00 UTC. Current status: adapter healthy, partial capacity restored, queue draining, cloud support provisioning temporary GPUs. Watch: pending pods, queue_length, adapter restart rate.

sre-ana: Acked, taking ownership for the remainder and will coordinate postmortem.

customer-success-lina: Noted. Will follow up with customers once final catch-up completed.

product-ops-claire: Thanks team. Meeting notes and timeline request posted to the incident doc. :+1:
